Subject: Strategic onramp credit request — Epsylon Health (VP/CFO authorization needed)

Team,

Epsylon Health is asking for an aggressive onramp concession to move a pilot to production. High level: they want a 40% credit applied to usage for the first 6 months to offset initial model tuning/throughput costs — their procurement flagged this as a must-have to clear legal and the board. The commercials they proposed are attached (epsylon_sow_v2.pdf) and there's a usage export showing token velocity for the last 30 days (expected_usage_report.csv).

Why this matters:
- Deal size if converted to a 12-month ARR profile is $420k ARR (conservative).
- Without the concession they will likely walk; with a limited credit we get a strong reference and a path to scale.

Risk concerns:
- 40% for 6 months materially reduces near-term recognized revenue and sets a precedent.
- We need to protect revenue recognition and avoid a permanent discount band.

Recommended structure for authorization (what I'm asking you to greenlight):
1) Approve a time-bound onramp credit up to 30% (not 40%) applied to net usage for the first 3 months, with the option to extend one additional month if customer hits milestone A (integration & perf SLA).
2) Include a clawback: if they don't reach $X usage by month 4 we recoup credits against future invoices.
3) Require a signed SOW amendment referencing the credit and usage floors.

I've flagged this as a VP/CFO decision because of the precedent and P&L impact. Attached is a quick pricing model I ran — happy to walk through numbers. Requesting quick take so I can respond to Daniel (they are asking for an answer this week).

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: epsylon_sow_v2.pdf (pdf), expected_usage_report.csv (csv)

Subject: Re: Strategic onramp credit request — Epsylon Health (VP/CFO authorization needed)

Jonas — thanks for the write-up. A couple of quick clarifying items before we elevate formally: 

- Can you confirm the expected ramp schedule (tokens/day) post-integration? I want to ensure our staged credits align to realistic milestones.
- Suggest we consider a stepped credit: 30% month 1, 20% month 2, 10% month 3. That reduces headline exposure and nudges them to accelerate usage.
- I'll attach the pricing-model.xlsx with a delta view (simple AR impact & payback window).

If we go the clawback route, legal wants the exact clawback mechanics (netting vs invoice credit vs DSRA). Also want an explicit do-not-exceed ceiling (for example: total credit not to exceed $75k).

Will loop in Sales Ops to ensure billing can handle staged credits.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing-model.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Strategic onramp credit request — Epsylon Health (VP/CFO authorization needed)

Appreciate the context. From Finance POV a few guardrails: 

- Approveability band: we can approve up to a 25% effective credit (net) without exec signoff if trade-offs are mitigated with firm usage milestones. Anything >25% requires CFO signoff.
- Revenue recognition: we need the SOW amendment to specify credits as a customer incentive (contra-revenue) so accounting can handle recognition appropriately.
- Suggested alternative: authorize a staged credit with a usage floor and a 12-month minimum commitment thereafter (if they convert to production). That preserves ARR while sharing initial risk.

If the ask is to reach the 40% headline, request is to move to formal exec escalation memo with explicit P&L impact and precedent rationale.

Karthik
Head of FP&A
Redwood Inference

Markus — forwarding our thread with a succinct recommended authorization for you to sign/route. Short summary below and a proposed memo block you can paste: 

Summary: Epsylon requests 40% for 6 months. We recommend a capped, time-bound compromise to protect revenue while getting the deal over the line.

Proposed authorization (for VP/CFO):
- Approve up to 30% onramp credit applied to billed usage for months 1–3.
- One-month extension (month 4) on approval by Sales & FP&A if milestone A is achieved (SLA + basic usage floor).
- Total credit cap not to exceed $60,000.
- Credits are subject to clawback (net against future invoices) if usage floors are not met by month 4.
- Require SOW amendment and signed commitment to a 12-month minimum if they elect to extend beyond pilot.

If you approve, please either sign the block below or request final CFO signoff (neha) if you want her to take it to the exec finance committee. I'm standing by to draft the SOW amendment for Legal.

Best,
Jonas
